name: Downtown Dubai
line: The city's address, around Burj Khalifa and The Dubai Mall.
intro: Downtown Dubai is Emaar's flagship district, built around Burj Khalifa, The Dubai Mall and the Dubai Fountain. Most homes are apartments, from compact studios to branded residences and full-floor penthouses, with the Boulevard tying the towers together on foot.
living: Burj Khalifa, The Dubai Mall and Dubai Opera on the doorstep
Walkable Boulevard with cafés, hotels and the fountain shows
Burj Khalifa/Dubai Mall metro station and Sheikh Zayed Road access
Business Bay and DIFC a few minutes away
buyers: Downtown suits buyers who want a trophy address with deep rental demand from short-stay and corporate tenants. Branded towers and fountain-view stacks hold a premium; older Old Town low-rises offer more space per dirham.

name: Business Bay
line: Canal-front towers next to Downtown, priced a step below it.
intro: Business Bay runs along the Dubai Water Canal directly south of Downtown, mixing residential towers, offices and hotels. It is one of the most actively traded districts in the city, with a deep pipeline of new launches beside established buildings such as the Peninsula and Executive Towers.
living: Canal promenade for walking, running and cycling
Downtown, Burj Khalifa and DIFC within minutes
Business Bay metro station and Al Khail Road access
Large choice of restaurants, gyms and hotel amenities
buyers: Business Bay rewards investors looking for yield close to Downtown, and end-users who want canal or Burj views for less than Downtown pricing. Office stock gives business owners a chance to buy their own premises.

name: Dubai Creek Harbour
line: Emaar's waterfront city on the historic creek.
intro: Dubai Creek Harbour is an Emaar master community on the banks of Dubai Creek, next to the Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary. Creek Beach, Creek Island and a long waterfront promenade give it a resort feel, ten minutes from Downtown and the airport.
living: Creek Beach and the Creek Island promenade
Views back to the Downtown skyline
Parks and cycle tracks across the master plan
Quick access to Dubai International Airport
buyers: Creek Harbour suits buyers who want new Emaar stock with waterfront views at a lower entry point than Downtown. Much of the pipeline is still under construction, so off-plan payment plans are widely available.

name: Dubai Hills Estate
line: Green, family-first living around a championship golf course.
intro: Dubai Hills Estate is a master community by Emaar and Meraas set around an 18-hole championship golf course, between Al Khail Road and Umm Suqeim Street. Villa clusters such as Sidra, Maple and the golf-front mansions sit alongside apartment districts close to Dubai Hills Mall.
living: Dubai Hills Mall and Dubai Hills Park
18-hole championship golf course
Schools and King's College Hospital within the community
Central location between Downtown and Dubai Marina
buyers: Dubai Hills suits families who want villas and townhouses with gardens close to the city, and buyers who value a well-run, finished master community. Golf-front and park-facing homes command a clear premium.

name: The Springs
line: Established lakeside townhouses with a neighbourhood feel.
intro: The Springs is one of Emaar's original Emirates Living communities: townhouses and villas set around a chain of lakes and landscaped walkways. Mature trees, community pools and the Springs Souk give it a settled, village atmosphere that newer communities take years to grow.
living: Lakes, parks and shaded walking paths
Springs Souk and nearby schools
Easy reach of Dubai Marina, JLT and Media City
Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road on either side
buyers: The Springs suits families upgrading from apartments and investors after steady long-term tenants. Lake-facing and upgraded units, especially larger layouts, are the most sought after.

name: Dubai Marina
line: Waterfront towers, the beach at JBR and a full city on foot.
intro: Dubai Marina is built around a man-made marina lined with high-rise residential towers, with Jumeirah Beach Residence and The Walk on the beachfront beside it. It is one of Dubai's most established rental markets, popular with professionals who want the beach, restaurants and transport in one place.
living: Marina Walk and the beach at JBR
Dubai Metro and Dubai Tram stations
Restaurants, yacht clubs and Bluewaters nearby
Media City and Internet City next door
buyers: The Marina suits investors who want reliable occupancy and buyers who want full-marina or sea views. Newer towers such as Marina Gate sit at the top of the market; older towers offer generous layouts at lower prices per square foot.
